criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Strong rationale and user identification, with references. However, no formal mission objectives/requirements (coverage, revisit, resolution, latency, lifetime, payload) are specified, so not complete.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt and task descriptions make plan feasible and link to launch/orbit/STK. But no contingency, dependencies, resource estimates, or explicit justification of plan against mission needs; information sources are listed separately.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
I will need to choose an optimal orbit path and altitude, and also calculate COEs & AOEs.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Only background reading and STK tutorials are reported; no design calculations, simulation outputs, trade studies, or quantitative results. This is minor progress, not sufficient technical evidence.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings, readable prose, consistent formatting, labelled Gantt, and footnoted sources. Some reference-list links are uncited/duplicated, and the figure lacks a formal caption, but presentation is strong.

technical_issues.issue: No formal mission requirements or performance specifications (coverage, revisit, resolution, spectral bands, data latency, lifetime, payload).
No actual preliminary technical work: no orbit/launch calculations, STK simulation results, link budget, power/thermal sizing, or COE/AOE values.
Gantt lacks contingencies, task dependencies, resource estimates, and explicit risk mitigation.
End-of-life option of 'leaving it where it is' is not consistent with space-debris best practice for LEO; deorbit or graveyard orbit should be justified.
Ocean acidification described as '30 percent more acidic' is imprecise; it is roughly a 30% increase in H+ concentration / ~0.1 pH decrease.
Some listed sources duplicate footnotes and are not cited in text; reference list and citations are not fully matched.

overall: Adequate preliminary report: mission rationale and Gantt are clear, but formal requirements and technical progress are weak. It needs STK/orbit/launch results, quantitative mission requirements, contingencies, and a cleaner reference list.

feedback.summary: Your report has a clear mission rationale and a readable, well-structured presentation. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, you need formal, quantitative mission requirements and real preliminary technical results, plus a more robust plan with contingencies and dependencies. Your presentation is already strong; tighten the reference list so every source is cited and matched.
next_steps: Add a formal requirements table in Mission Concept & Rationale covering coverage, revisit, resolution, spectral bands, data latency, lifetime and payload, each tied to user needs and cited where appropriate.

In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, include at least one quantitative preliminary result (e.g. STK orbit/coverage output, launch or link-budget calculation, power/thermal sizing) with brief interpretation, and add contingencies, task dependencies and resource estimates to the Gantt.
Revise the end-of-life plan to justify deorbit or a graveyard orbit for LEO, and clean up Useful Links so every listed source is cited in text and matches the reference list.

criteria.C1: You clearly explain why the Great Barrier Reef needs dedicated monitoring and identify users such as marine and conservation scientists. To reach Accomplished, add formal mission objectives and quantitative requirements—coverage, revisit, resolution, spectral bands, data latency, lifetime and payload—and link each to user needs with appropriate references. Also correct the ocean acidification wording to a ~30% increase in H+ concentration / ~0.1 pH decrease.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart and task descriptions make the plan believable and connect to orbit selection and STK work. To reach Accomplished, add contingencies, task dependencies and resource estimates, and explain why the plan is structured this way for this mission. Integrate information sources into the plan rather than listing them separately, and cite them where used.
criteria.C3: You report background reading and completion of STK tutorials 1–4, which shows useful preparation. To reach Accomplished, include actual preliminary technical results—for example STK orbit/coverage outputs, launch or link-budget calculations, power/thermal sizing, or COE/AOE values—with a brief description and interpretation. This will provide the evidence that you are on track for completion.
criteria.C4: Your headings, readable prose, consistent formatting and labelled Gantt chart make the report easy to follow. To secure the top level, add a formal caption to Image 1 and ensure every source in Useful Links is cited in the text and matches the reference list; remove duplicates and uncited links. Your presentation is already strong.
